finding: 3 exact duplicate rows found (rows 301-303, copying rows 16, 88, 151).
analytical_consequence: Artificially inflates sample size and can lead to biased model estimation.

finding: Age of -5 years found for patient 32.
interpretation: Clear data-entry error as negative age is impossible.
analytical_consequence: Biases age distribution and parameter estimates if left uncorrected.

finding: Age of 115 years found for patients 47, 93, 236.
interpretation: Physiologically extreme but possible; could also be a placeholder.
analytical_consequence: Can function as highly influential leverage points in regression models.
recommended_action: Retain but flag for sensitivity analysis in Chapter 05.

finding: Systolic BP of 280 mmHg found for patients 181, 209, 268.
interpretation: Physiologically extreme, representing severe hypertensive crisis or input error.
analytical_consequence: Outliers will distort blood pressure coefficients and linear assumptions.
recommended_action: Recode to NA or winsorize in Chapter 03.

finding: A1C of 1.5% found for patients 99, 172, 251 (two are diabetic).
interpretation: Biochemically impossible for a living human (normal range is 4-5.6%; diabetic is >6.5%).
analytical_consequence: Distorts A1C clinical significance in predictive models.

finding: Wait days of -3 found for patients 31, 112, 117, 132.
interpretation: Booking date recorded as after visit date, which is chronologically impossible.
recommended_action: Recode to 0 (interpreting as same-day scheduling lag) in Chapter 03.

finding: Casing mismatch: 5 rows contain lowercase 'medicaid' instead of 'Medicaid'.
interpretation: Simple case mismatch during data entry.
analytical_consequence: Splits one category into two separate levels in modeling, increasing parameters.
recommended_action: Convert all to Title Case 'Medicaid' in Chapter 03.

finding: Value mismatch: 5 rows contain abbreviation 'y' instead of 'Yes'.
analytical_consequence: Splits the positive response class into two levels, reducing group power.

finding: 8 blank string values found representing missing clinic locations.
analytical_consequence: Reduces sample size if complete-case analysis is used.
recommended_action: Recode blanks to 'Unknown' or impute in Chapter 03.

finding: 8 blank string values found representing missing visit reasons.
analytical_consequence: Reduces sample size if complete-case analysis is used.
recommended_action: Recode blanks to 'Unknown' or impute in Chapter 03.

finding: 8 NA values found in Body Mass Index.
analytical_consequence: Reduces sample size if complete-case analysis is used.
recommended_action: Impute using median or multiple imputation (MICE) in Chapter 03.

finding: 7 NA values found in A1C blood measure.
analytical_consequence: Reduces sample size if complete-case analysis is used.
recommended_action: Impute using median or multiple imputation (MICE) in Chapter 03.

finding: Severe class imbalance in RAW data (before deduplication, N = 303): 30 missed appointments (9.9%) vs 273 completed (90.1%); cleaned sample (N = 300) has 270 completed (90.0%) and 30 missed (10.0%).
interpretation: Severe class imbalance in the primary outcome variable.
analytical_consequence: Limits the degrees of freedom for modeling (overfitting risk; high events-per-variable constraint).
recommended_action: Restrict model complexity (limit predictor degrees of freedom) in Chapter 05.

finding: Rare outcome: only 1 'Yes' case out of 303 rows.
analytical_consequence: Cannot be modeled using logistic regression (unstable/singular models).
recommended_action: Treat descriptively only; do not model in regression.

finding: 6 post-outcome variables (satisfaction, costs, health improvement, etc.) included in raw predictors.
interpretation: Post-outcome variables cannot be used to predict the outcome itself.
analytical_consequence: Creates temporal leakage, artificially inflating predictive power.
recommended_action: Exclude post-outcome variables from predictor pool of primary model.
